title: A wing under a cover
hook: Some wings are hidden while an insect rests.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish beetle forewing covers from depicted hindwings.

misconception: The visible hard wing covers are always the beetle’s flight wings.
objective: Distinguish beetle forewing covers from depicted hindwings.

claims.text: Some wings are hidden while an insect rests. In the illustrated beetle with flight wings, what covers the folded hindwings while the beetle rests? The schematic shows hardened forewings called elytra covering the folded hindwings. In a beetle with functional flight wings, the hindwings can unfold; flight ability varies among beetles.
claims.source: Source leads for independent checking: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, https://naturalhistory.si.edu/research/entomology; OpenStax Biology 2e, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/28-3-superphylum-ecdysozoa. The precise supporting passages have not been checked.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: What are the hardened forewing covers of a beetle called? Elytra are the hardened beetle forewings.
